title: The Race of the Runaway Balloon
story: Thrashelmer the Gale Jaw, a whale-shaped storm beast, is chasing a runaway mail balloon carrying a sleeping baker. The balloon drifts at 12 miles per hour; Thrashelmer swims the wind at 20 miles per hour and is 24 miles behind. Mr 6, riding the balloon's rigging, does the math on his sleeve.
question: If Thrashelmer gains on the balloon at the difference of their speeds and starts 24 miles behind, how many hours until he catches up?
hint: How many miles does Thrashelmer close each hour? Use that gap-closing speed, not 20.
victory: Knowing he had exactly 3 hours, Mr 6 spent two of them steering into a warm updraft; Thrashelmer arrived at empty sky and got a faceful of cloud instead of a baker.
imagePrompt: A patchwork mail balloon high above golden clouds with a numeral-six knight clinging to the rigging, a vast whale-shaped storm beast churning through the wind far behind.
solution: Find the gap-closing speed: 28 − 20 = 8 miles closed each hour.
Divide the gap by that speed: 24 ÷ 8 = 3.
praise: Using distance ÷ speed was the right idea — the missing step was subtracting the speeds to get the chasing rate.
